clue.text: Drinking in college

definitions.meaning: first meaning: swallowing, as in knocking back a drink
second meaning: a college of Cambridge University

explanation.surface: A student spends their time boozing at university.
explanation.walkthrough: Downing is one of the colleges of Cambridge University.
explanation.definitionFit: To down a pint is to swallow it quickly, and Downing College is a Cambridge foundation.

clue.text: Cook said gluttony had bad effects

indicators.note: to cook something is to tamper with it, as with the books, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
gluttony is greed for food

explanation.surface: A chef remarks that overeating made people ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like the subject of 'said'; it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that disagreed with someone upset their stomach, which is having bad effects on them.

clue.text: Recording includes Welsh singer

indicators.note: something that includes another thing holds it within itself

parts.note: waxing is the old term for making a gramophone record
W is the abbreviation for Welsh

explanation.surface: A recording session features a singer from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh singer' reads as one phrase, but Welsh only supplies a letter and the singer is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The waxwing is a songbird, and in crosswords any bird may be called a singer.

clue.text: One changing a lot may be vain — or not

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could become something else entirely

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A reformer may or may not be conceited.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovator introduces new methods and ideas, so is someone constantly making changes.

clue.text: Pass the fish

definitions.meaning: first meaning
second meaning: a small spiny-finned fish

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like a request at dinner; the first word is the phrasal verb go by.
explanation.definitionFit: Time can go by, meaning pass, and the goby is a small fish found in rock pools.

clue.text: A swan, and two-thirds of a pig — some bird

indicators.note: taking two-thirds of a word means keeping four of its six letters and dropping the remaining third

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
a guinea pig, cut down to its first word

explanation.surface: A farmyard list: a swan and most of a pig, adding up to some sort of bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The pig is a guinea pig; its first word GUINEA loses its last two letters, leaving GUIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The penguin is a flightless seabird of the southern oceans, still classed among birds.

clue.text: Academic has tie that's loose

parts.note: short for professor
to ligate is to tie or bind, as a surgeon ties a vessel

explanation.surface: A professor wears his necktie undone.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose here means morally lax and dissolute, which is how a wasteful, debauched person is described.

clue.text: They are barely worth painting

parts.note: surface reading: hardly worth the bother of painting
setter's reading: bare subjects, people without clothes, thought fit to paint

explanation.definitionFit: Artists' studies of unclothed figures are a classic subject of oil painting.

clue.text: Keats's sweeter melodies not tried

definitions.meaning: first meaning: from Ode on a Grecian Urn, those melodies not heard are sweeter
second meaning: a legal case not yet heard in court

explanation.walkthrough: Keats wrote 'Heard melodies are sweet, but those ... are sweeter' in Ode on a Grecian Urn.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's line praises silent melodies, and a case that has never come before a judge remains unheard.

clue.text: Starts off neat and tidy, then yearns to be smartly dressed

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, the only ones kept here

parts.note: the opening letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: Someone who began tidy longs to dress smartly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is part of the surface only; the initials come from the next five words.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty is an informal adjective for neat and dapper in appearance.

clue.text: Musical instrument playing a sort of blue

parts.note: short for saxophone
a show that is playing is on

explanation.surface: A saxophone playing the blues.
explanation.walkthrough: Saxon blue is a pale greyish-blue dye colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxon blue is a named shade, originally a dye from Saxony, so the word qualifies a kind of blue.

clue.text: Dandy's showing a high temperature, and is inflamed

parts.note: a blood is an old word for a dandy or young rake, plus the 's
running hot

explanation.surface: A fop who is feverish and red in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: A blood is an old term for a fashionable young man about town.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodshot eyes are red and irritated, which is what inflamed describes.

clue.text: Sigh for the sound of armour

indicators.note: what something sounds like is how it is heard when spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a greave is a piece of armour protecting the shin

explanation.surface: A knight sighs wistfully for the clank of armour.
explanation.definitionFit: To grieve for someone is to mourn or pine for them, much as one sighs for a lost thing.

clue.text: Man admits defeat and demands some explanation

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: a man's name
a defeat is a loss

explanation.surface: A man concedes he lost and wants to know why.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is a list of terms with their meanings, which supplies explanation of difficult words.

clue.text: Guard gerbil — endlessly wandering pet

indicators.note: without an end means the last letter is cut off
wandering things stray from their place, so the letters move about

parts.note: taken as written
the word without its final letter

explanation.surface: Watch the gerbil, which keeps roaming about the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The budgie is a small Australian parakeet commonly kept as a household cage bird.

clue.text: People having a row can be private in the back

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rowing crew of that many oarsmen

definitions.note: a player in a rugby scrum, not a crew
definitions.meaning: second meaning, most likely: the rugby forward who packs down alone at the back of the scrum

explanation.surface: Quarrelling couples keep their arguments private at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having a row' suggests a quarrel, but it means rowing a boat. The second half's exact sense is uncertain; the best reading is rugby's number eight, a forward at the back of the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing boat crewed by that number of oarsmen is called by the numeral, and so is the rugby forward wearing that shirt number.

clue.text: Is a one-man-operated train open to attack?

definitions.note: describes the train, as an adjective would
definitions.meaning: first meaning, cryptic: a train run by the driver alone carries no guard
second meaning: undefended, vulnerable

explanation.surface: Asking whether driver-only trains leave passengers vulnerable.
explanation.walkthrough: On British railways the guard is the crew member at the back who handles doors; driver-only trains run without one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without protection lies exposed and vulnerable, and a train with no guard aboard is literally lacking one.

clue.text: How to resolve the claims of mediaeval enquirer

indicators.note: to resolve something can mean to break it down into parts and recombine them

parts.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A guide to settling the disputed assertions of a medieval scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval alchemists investigated matter, seeking to turn base metals into gold.

clue.text: Token tried, but bent — shame

parts.note: a disc can be a token, as used in a slot

indicators.note: something bent is twisted out of its shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone tried using a fake token, which was disgraceful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' looks like slang for crooked, fitting the fake token, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit someone brings disgrace upon them, the same sense as shame used as a verb.

clue.text: Unqualified for position on stage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: absolute, utter
second meaning: ..., the front of the stage on the actor's right

explanation.walkthrough: 'Unqualified' suggests lacking a qualification; here it means without reservation.
explanation.definitionFit: A downright lie is an utter, unreserved one, and down right is a stage direction toward the audience on the right.

clue.text: Campaign, and rations for it?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: military fighting

definitions.note: taken as war fare, food for a war
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split in two: the fare eaten in wartime

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the punning second meaning: food for fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A military campaign is armed conflict, and fare is food, so the war's fare would be its rations.

clue.text: Many a girl shows style

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Lots of young women display elegance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with class has elegance and flair, the same quality as style.

clue.text: Record rainbow over site of industry

parts.note: a rainbow is an arc of colour
a hive of industry, where busy bees work

explanation.surface: A record of a rainbow hanging over a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a stored collection of documents, kept as a historical record.

clue.text: Announce arrival of trains with ceremony

parts.note: to herald is to announce someone's coming
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A station announcer proclaims the trains with pomp.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldry also means pomp and colourful pageantry, the trappings of ceremonial occasions.

clue.text: Cuts wildly at the string

definitions.meaning: first meaning: chops roughly

definitions.note: a string of horses, read as plural
definitions.meaning: second meaning: riding horses, a string of them in a stable

explanation.walkthrough: A string is a group of horses kept together; hacks are ordinary riding horses.
explanation.definitionFit: To hack is to chop clumsily, and hacks are horses for hire forming a stable's string.

clue.text: Young Pooter found in bed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the son of Charles Pooter in The Diary of a Nobody
second meaning: a tall garden plant grown in a flower bed

explanation.walkthrough: The Diary of a Nobody is an 1892 comic novel by George and Weedon Grossmith; Pooter's son is called Lupin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lupin is the name of Pooter's son, and the lupin is a flowering garden plant.

clue.text: Could you call him a materialist, being in commerce? Right

definitions.text: Could you call him a materialist

indicators.note: letters that are in a longer word sit inside it, waiting to be lifted out

parts.note: the run of letters sitting inside this word
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Is a businessman just a materialist?
explanation.walkthrough: A materialist here is a dealer in materials, not someone obsessed with possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: A mercer is a dealer in textiles, especially silks, so he trades in cloth or fabric.

clue.text: Extra section for table takes two pages

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hinged or insertable flap that extends a table
second meaning: a single sheet of a book, printed on both sides

explanation.definitionFit: A table's extension board is called by this name, as is a book's sheet with a page on each side.

clue.text: Pretended a piece of glass is reported in the wine

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so the words are taken by how they sound

parts.note: sham means pretended or fake
a pane is a sheet of glass in a window

explanation.surface: Someone faked finding a shard of glass in their drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is a sparkling wine from the French region of that name.

clue.text: Ruinous in appearance, I was struggling

parts.note: taken as written
to vie is to compete or contend

explanation.surface: Someone looking a wreck explains they had been fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy grows over old ruins, so a building covered in it looks ancient and decayed.

clue.text: Educationalist of curious interest, almost

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
something curious is odd, so these letters come out in a strange order

parts.note: the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: A teacher whose ideas are of some odd interest.
explanation.walkthrough: Rudolf Steiner founded the Steiner (Waldorf) schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Steiner was an Austrian thinker whose educational theories founded the Waldorf schools.

clue.text: Those in best condition are ready to go to the match

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective used here as a noun, as in survival of the fittest

parts.note: fit as in fit and ready to play
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: The healthiest players are prepared for the big game.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a full international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: The fittest are those in the healthiest physical shape, as in Darwin's survival of the fittest.
